title: Demand Service Rate Programs: Step for the Account's Payment Record at Review
content:
*What does a good payment record add at review?*

Where the payments received in the window number at least 8 and the most recent invoice to fall due has
stood past its due day no longer than the tier's suspension period, a step of 0.15 is added. Where they
number at least 4 and the most recent invoice to fall due has stood past its due day no longer than the
tier's suspension period, a step of 0.08 is added. In any other case no step is added for the account's
payment record.

*Which suspension period?* The one published for the program the account holds under the Demand Service Rate Programs:

| Program | Suspension period (calendar days past due) |
|---|---|
| Time & Material Account | 45 |
| Priority Response Program | 45 |
| Block Hour Service Program | 45 |
| Emergency Response Program | 30 |
| Critical Facility Response Program | 30 |
| Dedicated Technician Program | 30 |

*The two conditions together.*

| Payments received in the window | The most recent invoice to fall due | The step |
|---|---|---|
| 8 or more | past its due day no longer than the tier's suspension period | 0.15 |
| 4 to 7 | past its due day no longer than the tier's suspension period | 0.08 |
| 4 or more | past its due day longer than the tier's suspension period | no step is added |
| fewer than 4 | any | no step is added |

*An illustration.* On the Emergency Response Program, whose suspension period is 30 calendar days, an
account with 8 payments in the window whose most recent invoice stands 30 days past its due day takes
the step of 0.15; with 7 payments it takes 0.08; and where that invoice stands 31 days past its due day
it takes no step at all, however many payments were received.
